label: Force into faction
summary: Forces the character to join a faction, on behalf of another character, for a set time.
details: The character joins even though they did not choose to. The one who forced them is named in forced_by. The duration is written in days, months or years; vanilla always uses years.

fields.name: faction
fields.text: The faction the character is forced into.

fields.name: forced_by
fields.text: The character who forces them to join.

fields.name: days / months / years
fields.text: How long the forced membership lasts.
fields.values: a number, written as days, months or years

label: Join faction, no checks
summary: Makes the character join the given faction without testing whether they are allowed to.
details: The normal join rule (the can_character_join trigger) is skipped. Runs on a character; the value is the faction.

label: Join organization
summary: Makes the character a member of the given organization.
details: Runs on the character who joins; the value is the organization.

label: Learn court language of
summary: Makes the character learn the court language of another character.
details: Runs on the learner; the value is the character whose court language is learned.

label: Learn language
summary: Makes the character learn the named language.
details: The value is a language key, for example language_latin or language_greek as vanilla writes them.

label: Learn culture's language
summary: Makes the character learn the language that the given culture speaks.
details: Runs on the learner; the value is a culture, often written as a link such as root.culture.

label: Lease to holy order
summary: Leases the title out to the given holy order.
details: Runs on a title. Any theocratic lease the title has is removed. Vanilla uses it a lot, with a holy order saved as a scope.

label: Leave culture era
summary: Makes the culture leave the given era and every era before it.
details: Runs on a culture. The value is a culture era type. The input shows no vanilla use, so the details rest on the game's documentation.

label: Leave faction
summary: Makes the character leave the given faction.
details: Runs on the character who leaves; the value is the faction.

label: Leave organization
summary: Makes the character leave their organization.
details: Written as `yes`. The game's documentation names no organization, so it takes none.

label: Log natural disaster
summary: Writes a log entry about the natural disaster situation it runs on.
details: Only writes anything when 'Logging.NaturalDisasters' was switched on in the console first. Write "started" or "ended". Run it after the situation's capital province and severity are set, so the entry is accurate.

label: Downgrade domicile building
summary: Lowers a building of the domicile by one level, or destroys it if it is already at the lowest level.
details: Runs on a domicile; the value is the building key. The game's documentation does not say what happens to the cost. A separate key, lower_domicile_building_no_refund, does the same without refunding.

label: Downgrade building, no refund
summary: Lowers a building of the domicile by one level, or destroys it if it is already at the lowest level, and pays nothing back.
details: Runs on a domicile; the value is the building key. Vanilla writes it with building names built from a template, such as a base name plus _03.

label: Strong claim
summary: Gives the character a strong claim on the title.
details: If the character has no claim on it yet, they get one. The title is the value.

label: Weak claim
summary: Gives the character a weak claim on the title.
details: If the character has no claim on it yet, they get one. The title is the value.

label: Make concubine
summary: Makes the target character a concubine of the character the effect runs on.
details: It runs on the character who takes the concubine; the value is the new concubine. The target should not be imprisoned.

label: Make holy site eminent
summary: Makes a holy site of the faith eminent.
details: Runs on a faith. The site must not be eminent already. Written either as just the holy site, or as a block that also names the acting character.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The holy site to make eminent.

fields.name: actor
fields.text: The character who does it.

label: Remove holy site eminence
summary: Makes a holy site of the faith no longer eminent.
details: Runs on a faith. The site must be eminent already. Written either as just the holy site, or as a block that also names the acting character.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The holy site to make not eminent.

fields.name: actor
fields.text: The character who does it.

label: Pregnant
summary: Makes the character pregnant by the given father.
details: No chance is involved. Run it on the mother. Vanilla always names a father; the number of children and the known-bastard flag are optional.

fields.name: father
fields.text: The real father of the child.
fields.values: a character, e.g. scope:father or root

fields.name: number_of_children
fields.text: How many children are born (twins and more).

fields.name: known_bastard
fields.text: Whether the child is publicly known as a bastard.

label: Pregnant, no checks
summary: Makes the character pregnant, without raising errors on things like celibacy.
details: The game's documentation lists the same fields as make_pregnant: the real father, the number of children and whether the child is a known bastard. The input shows no vanilla use of this key.

fields.name: father
fields.text: The real father of the child.

fields.name: number_of_children
fields.text: How many children are born.

fields.name: known_bastard
fields.text: Whether the child is a known bastard.

label: Story owner
summary: Makes the given character the new owner of the story.
details: Runs on a story. The value is the character who becomes its owner.

label: Activate trait
summary: Turns an inactive trait of the character on.
details: No tooltip is shown if the character cannot have the trait. Vanilla uses it for the genetic traits such as possessed_genetic.

label: Activate trait, show tooltip
summary: Turns an inactive trait of the character on.
details: Same as make_trait_active, but the tooltip is shown even if the character cannot have the trait.

label: Deactivate trait
summary: Turns a trait the character has off, without removing it.
details: No tooltip is shown if the character does not have the trait. Vanilla uses it for genetic traits such as possessed_genetic.

label: Deactivate trait, show tooltip
summary: Turns a trait the character has off, without removing it.
details: Same as make_trait_inactive, but the tooltip is shown even if the character does not have the trait.

label: Keep after death
summary: Keeps the character from being pruned (cleaned away by the game) after they die.
details: Written as `yes`. Everyone related to them is kept too, so use it with care. Only use it for someone who must stay around for several years after death.

label: Marry
summary: Marries the character to the target character.
details: Runs on one spouse; the value is the other.

label: Marry, matrilineal
summary: Marries the character to the target character in a matrilineal marriage.
details: Runs on one spouse; the value is the other. The game's documentation does not explain what matrilineal changes beyond the name, so what differs from a normal marriage is not confirmed here.

label: Recalculate participant groups
summary: Forces a new group to be worked out for every member of a situation participant group.
details: Written as `yes`. Every member's new group is calculated before any change is made. If a change for one person affects others' membership, switch that person's group first with a separate effect.

label: Move AI budget gold
summary: Moves gold from one of the AI's budget categories to another.
details: Never moves more than the source holds or the target has room for. The categories are budget_war_chest, budget_reserved, budget_short_term and budget_long_term.

fields.name: gold
fields.text: How much gold to move.

fields.name: from
fields.text: The budget it is taken from.

fields.name: to
fields.text: The budget it is put into.

label: Move AI budget treasury
summary: Moves treasury from one of the AI's budget categories to another.
details: Never moves more than the source holds or the target has room for. The categories are budget_war_chest, budget_reserved, budget_short_term and budget_long_term.

fields.name: treasury
fields.text: How much to move.

fields.name: from
fields.text: The budget it is taken from.

fields.name: to
fields.text: The budget it is put into.

label: Move domicile
summary: Moves the domicile to the given province.
details: Runs on a domicile. Vanilla mostly gives the capital province of some character.

label: Move custom title name
summary: Moves a custom title name from this title to the target title.
details: Runs on the title that has the custom name; the value is the title that receives it.

label: Move to the pool
summary: Makes the courtier or guest leave their court and move into the pool.
details: Written as `yes`. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Move to pool at province
summary: Makes the character leave their court, if they have one, and move into the pool of the given province.
details: Works on a courtier, a guest or a character already in the pool. The value is the province.

label: Multiply focus progress
summary: Multiplies focus progress.
details: The game documents nothing more: not what a focus is here, the value or the scope it runs on.

label: Open court position window
summary: Opens the window to appoint someone to a court position, with the character as the liege.
details: The value is the court position type. Vanilla uses it for the court physician and court astrologer.

label: Open interaction window
summary: Tries to open the window of a character interaction between an actor and a recipient.
details: The actor must be the current player. By default the actor and recipients are redirected; that only works when no secondary actor or recipient is set up or they are invalid.

fields.name: interaction
fields.text: The interaction to open.

fields.name: actor
fields.text: The character doing the interaction. Must be the current player.
fields.values: a character, e.g. scope:actor or root

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character it is aimed at.

fields.name: redirect
fields.text: Whether to redirect the actor and recipients.

fields.name: secondary_actor
fields.text: An extra character on the actor's side.

fields.name: secondary_recipient
fields.text: An extra character on the recipient's side.

fields.name: target_title
fields.text: A title the interaction is about.

label: Open window
summary: Tries to open the named window of the game's interface, without any scope data.
details: If the effect does not run through the interface, set the player, or the window opens for every player who runs it. A short form takes just the view name.

fields.name: view
fields.text: The window to open.

fields.name: view_message
fields.text: A view-specific instruction.

fields.name: player
fields.text: The player it opens for.

label: Open window with data
summary: Tries to open the named window of the game's interface, using the thing it runs on as the window's data.
details: For example a faith can be opened in the faith conversion window. If the effect does not run through the interface, set the player, or the window opens for every player who runs it. A short form takes just the view name.

fields.name: view
fields.text: The window to open.
fields.values: a view name, e.g. decision_detail or character

fields.name: view_message
fields.text: A view-specific instruction.

fields.name: player
fields.text: The player it opens for.

fields.name: data
fields.text: Extra data for the view. Vanilla gives a decision, a flag or an activity type.

fields.name: secondary_actor
fields.text: A second character the view is about. Vanilla uses it in some cases.
